text.tspan: unknown location → served. Use case: copyright /
licensing laws. Finer than country (city, ZIP)? Use a
third-party geolocation service or AWS WAF geo rules.
Without it: new content only after the TTL ends.
Invalidation = force a full or partial refresh,
bypassing the TTL: all files /* or a path /images/*
* must be the LAST character of the path
Next request → edge fetches the fresh copy
• First 1,000 invalidation PATHS per month are free (per AWS account, all distributions together); each path after that is charged.
• A wildcard path (/images/* or /*) counts as ONE path, even if it removes thousands of files.
• In progress at once: up to 3,000 files per distribution, or up to 15 wildcard paths.
• Best practice for frequent updates: versioned file names (app.v2.js, logo_2026.png) + long TTL. New name = new cache key, no invalidation
needed, no charge, and users never get a mix of old and new files.
• Exam: "users still see the old file after a deploy" → create an invalidation (or use versioned names).
